Simon Lifschutz lived in India for twenty-one years, during which time he revived industrial glass-making. These were the first studios in India to encourage young artists to work in ceramics and mosaics and create affordable work in an Indian idiom. They offered artists a livelihood and the freedom to develop their own style. Any artist was welcome to visit and work or teach there; prominent among them were K.H. Ara, K.K.
